In a GAN trained using the original minimax (saturating) generator objective, suppose the discriminator becomes nearly perfect very early in training. What will be the most likely consequence of this?
options: The generator learns faster because the discriminator provides perfect classification.
Both the generator and discriminator converge immediately to the optimal solution.
The generator's loss becomes zero, indicating perfect image generation.
The generator stops learning because it receives very small (vanishing) gradients.
questions.correct_answer: The generator stops learning because it receives very small (vanishing) gradients.

questions.text: A discriminative model and a generative model are trained on the same cat/dog dataset. Which statement is correct?
options: The discriminative model learns P(x); the generative model learns P(y|x).
The discriminative model learns P(y|x); the generative model learns P(x,y).
The generative model only learns a decision boundary.
questions.correct_answer: The discriminative model learns P(y|x); the generative model learns P(x,y).

questions.text: In RAG, a user asks a question using words that are very different from those used in the relevant document, but the underlying meaning is similar. Why can embedding-based retrieval still identify the relevant chunk?
options: Embeddings represent semantic information in a vector space, allowing similarity to be measured beyond exact word matching.
The underlying LLM extracts the keywords and their synonyms from the user's query.
FAISS automatically rewrites the query using the document's vocabulary.
The LLM searches the original document directly.
questions.correct_answer: Embeddings represent semantic information in a vector space, allowing similarity to be measured beyond exact word matching.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about transfer learning is/are correct?
options: Transfer learning reduces the amount of labeled data required for many tasks.
Freezing layers prevents their weights from being updated during backpropagation.
Transfer learning is useful only for image classification tasks.
A pre-trained model always achieves higher accuracy than a model trained from scratch.
correct_answer: Transfer learning reduces the amount of labeled data required for many tasks.
Freezing layers prevents their weights from being updated during backpropagation.

The projection layer contains 24,576 weights across all patches.
